steps.title: Import React and create the main App component
steps.instruction: Import React from 'react' and create a functional component named App that returns a basic div element.
steps.hint: Start by importing React, then define your component. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a React component ready to build upon for the micro-frontends lesson.
successCriteria: React is imported from 'react' and an App component is created that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and created the App component. This is the foundation for building micro-frontends.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've both imported React and created an App component that returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to import React from 'react' and create an App component that returns a div element.

steps.title: Create a ProductCard component
steps.instruction: Create a separate functional component named ProductCard that takes product data as props and returns a div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called ProductCard that accepts props as its parameter and returns JSX.
steps.seedCode:
// Import React and create the App component here

// Create the ProductCard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ProductCard component is defined and ready to receive product data.
successCriteria: The ProductCard component is created as a function that accepts props and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the ProductCard component. This demonstrates component isolation, a key concept in micro-frontends where each component can be developed independently.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've defined a function named ProductCard that takes props and returns a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductCard component isn't defined correctly. Check that you've created a function named ProductCard that accepts props and returns JSX.

steps.title: Create a ShoppingCart component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ShoppingCart that manages its own cart items state using useState.
steps.hint: Define a component that initializes state for cart items and returns a container element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ShoppingCart component with its own state for cart items is created, demonstrating independent feature component design.
successCriteria: ShoppingCart component is defined with useState for cart items and returns a div container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a ShoppingCart component with its own state, which is a key pattern in micro-frontends for independent feature components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a ShoppingCart component that uses useState for cart items and returns a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ShoppingCart component isn't defined correctly. Create a functional component named ShoppingCart with useState for cart items.

steps.title: Initialize cart state in ShoppingCart
steps.instruction: Inside the ShoppingCart component, use the useState hook to initialize a state variable named 'cartItems' as an empty array.
steps.hint: Import useState if not already imported, then call useState([]) inside the component to create the state variable and setter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: state initialization
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The ShoppingCart component will have a cartItems state variable initialized to an empty array, ready to store cart items.
successCriteria: The ShoppingCart component contains a useState call that initializes cartItems as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the cart state. The cartItems array is now ready to store products added to the cart.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] as the initial value, and naming the variable 'cartItems'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ShoppingCart component doesn't have the cartItems state initialized correctly. Remember to use useState([]) inside the component.

steps.title: Add addToCart handler in ShoppingCart
steps.instruction: Inside the ShoppingCart component, create a function named addToCart that takes a product object as a parameter and adds it to the cartItems state array.
steps.hint: Define the function inside the component, above the return statement. Use the setCartItems function to update the state by adding the new product to the existing array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ShoppingCart component now has an addToCart handler function that can be called to add products to the cart state.
successCriteria: The addToCart function is defined inside the ShoppingCart component, takes a product parameter, and updates the cartItems state by adding the new product.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the addToCart handler function. This function will allow products to be added to the cart state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly updates the cartItems state by adding the new product to the existing array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addToCart function is missing or doesn't properly update the cartItems state. Remember to create a function that takes a product parameter and adds it to the state array.

steps.title: Create product data in App component
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, create a products array containing at least two sample product objects. Each product should have id, name, and price properties.
steps.hint: Define the array directly in the component body (not inside JSX). Use numeric IDs, string names, and numeric prices.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will have a products array ready to pass to other components.
successCriteria: A products array is defined in the App component with at least two product objects containing id, name, and price.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've prepared the product data that will be shared across micro-frontend components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the products array. Make sure it contains at least two complete product objects with id, name, and price properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The products array isn't properly defined. Create an array of product objects inside the App component.

steps.title: Add ProductCard components to App markup
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, map through the products array to render a ProductCard component for each product.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the products array. For each product, return a ProductCard component with appropriate props.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component will display ProductCard components for each product in the products array.
successCriteria: The products array is mapped to render ProductCard components with appropriate props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the products array to render ProductCard components, demonstrating component composition in a micro-frontend architecture.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the map method on the products array and returning a ProductCard component for each product.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mapping logic is missing or incorrect. Remember to use the map method on the products array to render ProductCard components.

steps.title: Add ShoppingCart component to App markup
steps.instruction: Add the ShoppingCart component to the App JSX, placing it after the product cards section.
steps.hint: You can add the ShoppingCart component as a JSX element <ShoppingCart /> inside the return statement.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now includes the ShoppingCart component in its rendered output, demonstrating independent component integration in a micro-frontend architecture.
successCriteria: ShoppingCart component is added as a JSX element in the App return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully integrated the ShoppingCart component alongside the product cards, showing how micro-frontends can combine independent components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to add the ShoppingCart component as a JSX element in the App's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ShoppingCart component needs to be added to the App JSX. Look for where you should place component elements in the return statement.

steps.title: Add Add to Cart button to ProductCard
steps.instruction: Inside the ProductCard component, add a button with the text 'Add to Cart' that calls the onAddToCart prop function when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick handler that calls the onAddToCart prop function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ProductCard component now includes a button that, when clicked, triggers the onAddToCart function passed as a prop.
successCriteria: Button's onClick calls the onAddToCart prop function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the Add to Cart button with the click handler, enabling cross-component communication.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the button has the correct text and the onClick handler calls the onAddToCart prop function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or click handler is missing or incorrect. Review the ProductCard component structure and prop usage.

steps.title: Wire ProductCard button to ShoppingCart handler
steps.instruction: In the ProductCard component, add an onClick handler to the button that calls the onAddToCart prop with the product object.
steps.hint: Use the onClick attribute on the button element and pass a function that calls onAddToCart(product).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button click to a handler
<button onClick={() => handleAction(item)}>Do Action</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The Add to Cart button will trigger the addToCart function from ShoppingCart when clicked, passing the product data.
successCriteria: The button has an onClick handler that calls onAddToCart with the product object as argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully connected the ProductCard button to the ShoppingCart handler, demonstrating loose coupling between micro-frontends.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added an onClick handler, but make sure it calls onAddToCart with the product object as argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button click isn't properly wired to the handler. Add an onClick attribute that calls onAddToCart(product).
